title: Dialysis Patient Transport — Partner Unit Availability

transcript.speaker: Beth Kowalczyk, RN
transcript.text: Dr. Shah, it's Beth Kowalczyk from dialysis. I've reached all nine outpatients. Four missed treatment Thursday and are due today. One, Mr. Brandt, had a potassium of 6.1 last week and was on the edge. Two live alone with no ride, and one is in a wheelchair. The partner unit in the suburbs—Westgate Dialysis Center in Maumee—has six open chairs tomorrow from 06:00 and two today at 14:00. I need to know who goes first and how we get them there.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Anita Shah
transcript.text: Beth, prioritize the four who missed treatment and Mr. Brandt with the high potassium. The others can go tomorrow. Book the two today slots at 14:00 for them. Use Social Work to arrange wheelchair vans for the two who live alone. Call the partner unit's physician to confirm availability and send the secure fax with patient records.

transcript.speaker: Beth Kowalczyk, RN
transcript.text: Understood. I’ll book the two 14:00 slots now. Social Work will handle transport. I’ll send the secure fax to St. Joseph's with all records.

instructorNote: This inject tests the decision-making authority of the Dialysis Medical Director and the coordination between clinical and support teams for patient transport under water advisory constraints.
